unmapped_findings: Experimental AGS evolution for the 950→1050 °C (ε_I=0.2) sample: AGS drops to a minimum near 0.5 strain and then increases again toward 0.9 strain; the 3D CA simulated curve flattens above 75 μm (Fig. 16d; b0207, figure_016).

Simulated DRX fraction evolution (Fig. 24b): for 950→1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1, ε_I=0.2, the total DRX fraction rises steeply near strain 0.25–0.3; the first-stage fraction peaks near the 0.6 gridline around strain 0.3 then falls to near zero by strain 0.6 (figure_024).

At a comparable total DRX fraction (~45% at 0.23 strain) with the constant 1050 °C condition, matrix grains A, B, C of this increasing-temperature sample retain higher dislocation density (1×10¹¹–1.240×10¹⁴ m⁻² vs 1×10¹¹–3.067×10¹³ m⁻²), which drives rapid DRX growth (Fig. 26; b0242).

For the 950→1050 °C (ε_I=0.2) case, the unmodified Model 1 delayed the predicted post-transient stress softening, while Model 2 and the 3D CA reproduced the experimental stress decrease (Fig. 9c vs 9d; b0188).

This sample corresponds to a transient decrease of the Zener-Hollomon parameter Z_P (temperature rise); unlike a transient Z_P increase, the transient decrease leaves little change in the final AGS relative to the corresponding constant condition (Table 7; b0252).
